text: The legacy key splits as the Work Package fixes: RWB-P1-E1069-APP owns the 30 view definitions, the two view migrations, the three helper functions (inside the Section A migration, per TSD P1 T3.2), the conformance test, the dictionary assertions and the read contract; RWB-P1-E1069-DB owns the rwb_source_data login, the grant block, the view owner ace_view_owner and the four extension tables; RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG proves the 19-login grant matrix and both halves of boundary rule BND-6. The 30 views stay in schema recovery, owned by ace_view_owner, because they read ACE's own tables, and each service's own tables sit in its own rwb_* schema (DP-01, DP-05, ADR-010).
why: No source splits one legacy story three ways, and the split decides which story writes which statement and which test proves it; the story cannot be written and cannot be kept true against the rwb-access and integration slices without a stated division.

text: The ACE read of rwb-source-data is one REST contract on base /api/recovery/source-data/v1 (Architecture v5 slides 15 and 41), and every other service and every agent reaches ACE data only through it, one hop with a 2 s client budget (DP-05, DP-11); a Temporal caller uses an activity on the rwb-source-data task queue. AceSourceReadRepository stays an internal repository of the owning service and is not the cross-service path.
why: Architecture v5 and TSD P1 give two different shapes for the same read, and the shape decides whether the 18 other services have a contract to build against or a shared jar.

impact: If the TSD wording were kept, the other services would import a jar and the one-hop rule and the 2 s budget would move into the caller; no view, grant or extension table changes.

text: The login of this service is rwb_source_data (Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29); the platform DB story RWB-PLT-NF06-DB creates the 19 logins and their schemas, so this story asserts the login and issues its grants rather than creating a second login, and the credential and its rotation policy stay with the platform DB owner and never appear in a migration, a script or a runbook.
why: The legacy story assumes the role exists and says nothing about who creates it or who holds the credential, and a migration that carries a password would put a secret in a repository.

text: The grant block of legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 is reused as written, with the schema fixed to recovery (no recoverySchema token) and the role recovery_svc renamed rwb_source_data; ace_view_owner keeps USAGE on schema public and SELECT on the 21 Tier 1 tables named in the legacy section 11, and gains SELECT on the 14 Tier 2 tables once RWB-ACE-001 lands; each view is granted one at a time, PUBLIC is revoked on all tables of schema recovery, and no GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES is written.
why: The legacy grant block is the only enumeration of the grantee list, and the target renames the role and fixes the schema; the 21 against 22 count conflict must be resolved without inventing a table name.

text: This Day-1 database story runs on rwb-source-data's per-service Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline; its three migrations are ordered extension tables, Section A grant, Section B grant, with the two view migrations of RWB-P1-E1069-APP between them, and the exact version numbers are assigned by the sequence owner at build time. RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is recorded in section 13 as a note and not as a metadata build dependency, because the Work Package fixes 'Depends on (build)' as None for this story and a Day-1 story carries no H.
why: A grant cannot be written before the view it grants on exists, and the two slices share one sequence, so the order must be stated even though neither story depends on the other's build; the Day-1 rule of Template and Rules R5.7 fixes the metadata row as None.

text: Boundary rule BND-6 is written once, over this service's package, in RWB-P1-E1069-APP's build, with the 30 view names in recovery-modules.yaml as the only allowed source objects; the database slice holds no rule code. The second half of the boundary, no v_ace_* view named outside rwb-source-data and no other service's schema named, together with the grant matrix across the 19 logins, is proven in RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG.
why: One legacy rule now guards 19 services, and no single service can read the other 18 schemas or hold 19 logins to prove it; the rule must be stated once in the owning service and proven once in the integration slice.
